title: Unified Inference v23 \n\nProduct Overview, PRD, Design Spec, Roadmap & Pricing
author: Ava Martinez
summary: Comprehensive product document for Unified Inference v23 covering the product overview, PRD and requirements, technical design specs, roadmap and themes, pricing & packaging updates, and release notes and rollout plan.
content:
Overview:

Summary:
Unified Inference v23 is the next major release of Redwood's unified inference platform. v23 focuses on three primary goals: (1) improved cost-efficiency through request-aware batching and adaptive quantization, (2) narrower p99 latency tail via pre-emptive KV-cache warming and model variant fast-failover, and (3) clearer packaging/price tiers that map to Hosted, Dedicated, and Private customers. v23 is intended to be backward-compatible with the existing API surface while adding opt-in controls for advanced performance controls.

Business goals (top-level):
- Reduce average per-token cost for typical webchat workloads by 18-25% versus v21 baseline.
- Reduce p99 text-generation latency by 20% on standard 2048-context workloads.
- Increase upgrade/rollout adoption across Dedicated customers to 70% within 60 days of GA.
- Launch new pricing tiers (Optimize and Enterprise Plus) and achieve 12% attach rate for Optimize within Q1 post-GA.

Target customers and use-cases:
- AI-native startups seeking lower per-token cost for high-throughput assistants.
- Mid-market SaaS teams requiring predictable p99 latency for interactive products.
- Regulated customers using Private deployments who need quantization profiles and KMS integration.

Product scope (in-scope):
1) Serving runtime enhancements: adaptive quantization profiles by workload, pre-emptive KV-cache warming for hot prefixes, continuous micro-batching improvements.
2) Model routing: fine-grained routing policies (latency/cost/region/tier), automated fast-failover to compatible model variants.
3) Control plane and Console: per-route batching controls, quantization profile selector, rollout instrumentation and migration helpers.
4) Pricing & Packaging: new Optimize SKU (cost-optimization toolkit) and Enterprise Plus (SLA + extended retention).

Out of scope (for v23):
- Major API surface changes (new endpoints). Minor ergonomic SDK updates allowed.
- New private deployment install mechanisms beyond existing on-prem packages.

Product Requirements (PRD):

1. Functional requirements (MUST):
- FR-001: Adaptive quantization profiles must reduce fp16 token compute by enabling int8/int4 routes for supported models without manual customer tuning.
  - Acceptance criteria: end-to-end tests show >=15% GPU memory reduction and no >2% delta in top-1 token-match quality on benchmark prompt set.
- FR-002: Per-route batching controls in Console and API (enable/disable, target batch size, latency SLO guardrails).
  - Acceptance criteria: console control available; API returns current batching config; automations respect guardrails.
- FR-003: Pre-emptive KV-cache warming for prefix patterns with configurable TTLs and hit-rate metrics surfaced in Console.
  - Acceptance criteria: integrated metric with 95th percentile estimation; warm-up improves p50 token latency for warmed prefixes by >=10%.
- FR-004: Fast-failover routing to model variants when instance health or capacity constraints are detected, with automatic rollback on quality regression.
  - Acceptance criteria: failover occurs within 300ms of health trigger and rollback initiated when quality regression threshold exceeded.

2. Non-functional requirements (SHOULD):
- NFR-001: p99 latency reduction target: 20% improvement over v21 for 2048-context standard workload in benchmark lab.
- NFR-002: Observability: per-request tracing to link batching decisions, routing choice, quantization profile, and model version.
- NFR-003: Backwards-compatibility: existing SDK clients should operate without mandatory changes; new features are opt-in.

3. Security and compliance requirements (MUST):
- SR-001: All quantization artifacts and model variant mappings must be audited and logged.
- SR-002: Private deployments must support KMS/HSM key rotation without service interruption (planned maintenance allowed with pre-notice).

4. Operational requirements (MUST):
- OR-001: CI performance gating: PRs that modify serving runtime must run the benchmark suite with p50/p95/p99 checks; commits failing thresholds blocked.
- OR-002: Runbooks created for cache-warmup failures, quantization regression, and fast-failover incidents.

Design Specification (technical):

High-level architecture changes:
- Quantization Layer: introduce an adaptive quantization selector that lives in the model dispatch path. It consults a lightweight cost/quality model (offline-trained heuristics) that maps workload fingerprints to suggested quantization profiles (e.g., int8-fp16 hybrid, int4 aggressive). Profiles are stored in the config service and versioned.

- KV-cache warming: add a warmup worker that observes traffic patterns and enqueues prefix warm tasks. Warming uses lightweight warm instances with cached KV states seeded from snapshot diffs. Warm instances do not serve customer traffic until health checks pass.

- Batching improvements: continuous micro-batching will be extended to support per-route target batch sizes and time-budgeted batching (e.g., maximum latency budget overrides target batch size).

Detailed components and owners:
- Adaptive Quantization Selector (owner: eng-serving-runtime / Marco Alvarez)
  - Inputs: workload fingerprint, model metadata, historical quality metrics.
  - Outputs: quantization profile id, expected memory/cost delta.
- Warmup Worker (owner: eng-platform / Leah Chen)
  - Inputs: prefix frequency table, TTL config, warm concurrency limits.
  - Outputs: warm tasks, warm health metrics.
- Routing & Fast-Failover (owner: eng-infra / Rohit Singh)
  - Integration with existing smart router; new health signals and rollback triggers.
- Console & Telemetry (owner: eng-developer-experience / Nina Park)
  - UI surfaces for per-route batching controls and quantization profile selection; new dashboards and alert rules.

API changes and examples (backwards-compatible):
- GET /v1/routes/{route_id}/batching-config -> returns {"enabled": true, "target_batch_size": 8, "latency_budget_ms": 150}
- PATCH /v1/routes/{route_id}/batching-config -> body supports {"target_batch_size", "latency_budget_ms", "enabled"}
- New optional query param on generate endpoint: quantization_hint=profile_id (customers can explicitly request a profile; default behavior is platform-selected)

Telemetry and metrics (minimum set):
- quant_profile.selected (tag: profile_id, route, model)
- batch.size (histogram by route)
- warm.prefix.hit_rate (by prefix pattern)
- failover.count (by source cause)
- p50/p95/p99 latency broken down by batching decision and quantization profile

Acceptance criteria and testing plan:
- Unit & integration tests for the quantization selector with synthetic fingerprints.
- Regression harness: run eval set of 50k prompts and ensure quality deltas <=2% for top-1 match across supported models.
- Performance lab: 3x run under representative traffic (chat, long-context generation) to validate p99/p95 targets.
- Beta customer program (Dedicated + Hosted) with 6 customers running opt-in features for 8 weeks and providing usage/quality feedback.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Alpha: internal canary (2 weeks) - internal teams only, extra logging enabled.
2) Beta: invite-only Dedicated customers and Hosted early adopters (8 weeks) - provide migration guide, dedicated support channel.
3) GA: platform-wide opt-in release (4 weeks) - feature flags enabled by default for new routes, existing routes remain opt-in for 60 days, then auto-evaluation to suggest enablement.

Rollout steps (detailed):
- Pre-rollout: create canary fleet, configure additional autoscaling policies, pre-populate quantization profiles.
- Day-0: enable feature-flagged path for <1% of traffic; validate telemetry and failover behavior.
- Day-7: expand to 10% if no regression; begin beta on invited customers.
- Day-21: expand to 50% with monitoring and automated rollback hooks.
- Day-60: GA decision and enable opt-in suggestions in Console; communicate to customers.

Operations runbooks (short pointers):
- Cache-warmup-failure.md: steps to re-seed snapshots, recycle warm instances, and increase warm concurrency thresholds.
- Quantization-regression.md: steps to rollback to safe profiles, revert profile mapping, and open a P0 regression ticket.
- Fast-failover-loop.md: instructions to inspect health signals, quarantine a variant, and manually route traffic.

Roadmap & Themes (quarterly):
- Q4 2027 (v23 GA target): Adaptive quantization, KV-cache warming, per-route batching controls, new Optimize SKU pilot.
- Q1 2028: Consolidate quality monitoring, auto-suggestion engine for routes, SDK ergonomics for quantization hints.
- Q2 2028: Integrations: expanded model catalog support, GPU-specific kernel tuning, and additional pricing experiments for cost guarantees.

Pricing & Packaging notes (product and finance collaboration):
- SKU definitions (high level):
  - Hosted Standard (unchanged): per-token pricing with baseline latency SLO.
  - Optimize (new): add-on tier for cost-optimization tools (per-route recommendations, auto-quantization, extended batching policies). Pricing: additional 10% of token spend as a management fee or $0.02 per 1k tokens (smaller customers can choose higher fixed fee).
  - Enterprise Plus (new): SLA 99.95% uptime, 1-hour on-call support, 90-day telemetry retention, prioritized rollout windows. Pricing: uplift on Dedicated commits (negotiated) + platform fee.

- Packaging guidance: Optimize is enabled per-route; customers can trial Optimize on a single route for 30 days free. Enterprise Plus bundled with Dedicated reserved capacity contracts.

- Billing events: quantization-driven savings will be reflected in per-token utilization; Optimize management fee billed monthly. Detailed billing lines added: quant_profile_savings_override and optimize_fee.

Release notes (v23-alpha -> v23-GA):
- v23-alpha (2027-11-20): internal canary; introduced experimental quantization selector and observability events.
- v23-beta (2027-11-30): beta customers onboarded; console controls for per-route batching; warmup worker soft-launch.
- v23-rc1 (2027-12-08): fixed regressions in int4 aggressive profiles, improved warm snapshot diff size by 40%.
- v23-GA (planned 2027-12-20): targeted GA date. Key user-facing changes: per-route batching controls in Console, quantization profile selector, Optimize SKU pilot, improved p99 latency and cost savings.

Known risks and mitigations:
- Risk: aggressive quantization can cause subtle quality regressions for rare prompts.
  - Mitigation: conservative default profiles, automatic rollback thresholds, and mandatory beta for int4 aggressive.
- Risk: warmup worker misconfiguration could increase cost without latency benefit.
  - Mitigation: safe defaults, cost budget checks, and warmup dry-run telemetry.
- Risk: customer confusion over new pricing SKUs.
  - Mitigation: clear console messaging, 30-day trials, and sales/CS enablement docs.

Open questions (for leadership / product council):
- Q1: What is the acceptable minimum attach rate for Optimize to consider GA billing? (recommended: 10% within 90 days)
- Q2: For Enterprise Plus, should telemetry retention be configurable per-customer beyond 90 days as an add-on?

Appendices:
A. Acceptance test matrix (short):
- Perf lab scenarios: chat (latency-sensitive), long-context summarization, high-throughput embedding+reranking.
- Quality eval: 50k prompt pairs across supported models, automated diff and human spot-checking for regressed prompts.

B. Customer migration checklist (for solutions engineering):
1) Identify candidate routes and traffic patterns.
2) Run recommended benchmark on staging with quantization profiles.
3) Enable Optimize on route in trial mode and monitor warm.prefix.hit_rate and quality signals for 2 weeks.
4) Confirm SLA and billing preferences with account team.
